# SPD-090 — Bash hook: git bugreport and git diagnose with no -o write their report into the current directory, unchecked

## Brief
SPD-049 checks the path these verbs name with -o or --output-directory, but with neither option git writes the report into the directory the shell is in, and the hook models no target at all. A member in the ledger root leaves git-bugreport-<date>.txt or git-diagnostics-<date>.zip in a directory outside its deliverables, and Spud leaves one past Law 1. The file name carries a timestamp git chooses, so the hook would have to model the directory rather than the file, which is why SPD-049 left it: a directory target reads as an empty repository path in the path rule's reason and wants its own shape.

Evidence: Probed on git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157) in this worktree, SPD-049: 'git bugreport -s spd049' printed "Created new report at 'git-bugreport-spd049.txt'" and left that file in the worktree root, and 'git diagnose -s spd049' left git-diagnostics-spd049.zip beside it (both removed afterwards; they appeared in git status as untracked). With -o the path goes through the path rule since SPD-049 (tests/test_hooks.py GitFileWriteTest.test_the_other_verbs_that_name_a_path_they_write). Fix sketch: give syntax.GIT_VERB_FILE_OPTIONS a default target per verb -- the directory the shell is in, named in the reason as the directory rather than a file -- or refuse a member the two verbs outright, since neither is work a member needs.
